audience: IELTS candidates and English learners in Uzbekistan, mostly teenagers and young adults at B1-C1 level aiming for band 6.5-8.

style.voice: A clear, practical IELTS teacher. Very short lines, simple explanations, no long paragraphs, no hype. British spelling.
extra_rules: Layout must copy the example post exactly: a title line, then short labelled sections. Each section starts with ONE emoji and a short bold label on its own line, followed by very short lines. Leave a blank line between sections. No long paragraphs, no bullet symbols.
Always include these sections near the end, in this order: the Uzbek section, '📝 IELTS tip' (one sentence), '❓ Mini task' (one question or tiny task ending with 👇).
Do not write the channel name or @handle; it is added automatically.
Never promise to check, correct or reply to comments. You may invite students to write a sentence, but do not say anyone will check it.

Avoid cliche 'IELTS word list' vocabulary that every prep channel already teaches, such as: paramount, detrimental, conducive, plethora, myriad, crucial, pivotal, ubiquitous, delve, meticulous, beneficial, significant, nowadays, a double-edged sword, a piece of cake, in a nutshell, every coin has two sides. Choose fresher items that fluent writers and speakers really use: precise verbs, natural collocations, and current expressions from quality journalism.
example_posts: 📘 Word of the Day: SCARCE 🔤 Part of speech Adjective 📖 Meaning Scarce = rare, limited, or not enough in quantity, especially when something is hard to find. 🧠 In simple words: 👉 there is very little of it. 🗣 Examples Clean drinking water is scarce in some regions. Jobs were scarce during the economic crisis. Food became scarce after the disaster. 🧩 Common collocations scarce resources scarce supply scarce opportunities in scarce supply 💡 Register ✔️ Neutral to formal ✔️ Common in news, academic writing, and IELTS answers 🇺🇿 Uzbek scarce — камёб, етарли бўлмаган, танқис 📝 IELTS tip Use scarce instead of not enough to sound more academic and precise. ❓ Mini task What resource is becoming scarce in the modern world? 👇

monday.title: IELTS Vocabulary
monday.brief: Word of the Day, in EXACTLY the format and section order of the example post (Part of speech, Meaning, In simple words, Examples x3, Common collocations x3-4, Register, Uzbek, IELTS tip, Mini task). Title: 'Word of the Day: WORD' with the word in capitals. Choose ONE useful band 6.5-7.5 word for common IELTS topics (environment, education, health, technology, work, cities, society). The topic label must be ONLY the word itself.

tuesday.title: Grammar Tips
tuesday.brief: ONE grammar point that improves the Grammatical Range and Accuracy score (e.g. a conditional type, relative clauses, passive, inversion, articles, a tense contrast, cleft sentences, participle clauses). Title: 'Grammar Tip: NAME'. Sections: 📖 Rule (one or two lines), 🧠 In simple words, 🗣 Examples (3), ⚠️ Common mistake (one ❌ wrong line and one ✅ correct line), then Uzbek (translate the key rule in one line), IELTS tip, Mini task.

wednesday.title: IELTS Speaking
wednesday.brief: Rotate between Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3. Title: 'IELTS Speaking: Part N'. Sections: ❓ Question (one realistic exam question or cue card), 🗣 Sample answer (band 7+, 3-5 short sentences), 🧩 Useful phrases (3-4 taken from the answer), 💡 Strategy (one line), then Uzbek (translate the useful phrases), IELTS tip, Mini task. State the part and the question in the topic label.

thursday.title: Common English Mistakes
thursday.brief: ONE common mistake per post, ideally typical for Uzbek and Russian speakers (prepositions, articles, word order, false friends, countable/uncountable, confusing word pairs). Title: 'Common Mistake: SHORT NAME'. Sections: ❌ Wrong (one sentence), ✅ Correct (one sentence), 📖 Why (one or two lines), 🗣 More examples (3 correct sentences), then Uzbek (explain why learners make it, one line), IELTS tip, Mini task. Name the exact mistake in the topic label.

friday.title: Advanced Vocabulary
friday.brief: Advanced Word of the Day, in EXACTLY the format and section order of the example post (Part of speech, Meaning, In simple words, Examples x3, Common collocations x3-4, Register, Uzbek, IELTS tip, Mini task). Title: 'Advanced Word of the Day: WORD' with the word (or short expression) in capitals. Choose ONE C1-C2 item that students are unlikely to know from typical IELTS word lists: a precise verb, a strong collocation or an expression used in quality journalism. The topic label must be ONLY the word or expression itself.

saturday.title: IELTS Reading Tips
saturday.brief: ONE practical strategy for ONE question type (True/False/Not Given, Yes/No/Not Given, matching headings, matching information, sentence or summary completion, multiple choice, short answers) or ONE skill (skimming, scanning, time management, paraphrase spotting, unknown words). Title: 'IELTS Reading Tip: NAME'. Sections: 📖 The idea (one or two lines), 🧠 In simple words, 🪜 Steps (3-4 numbered short lines), ⚠️ Common trap (one line), then Uzbek (the key idea in one line), IELTS tip, Mini task.

sunday.title: Interesting English Facts
sunday.brief: ONE surprising and well-documented fact about English (word origins, odd spellings, history of the language, numbers about English, unusual words, British vs American differences). Title: 'English Fact: SHORT NAME'. Sections: 🤔 Did you know? (the fact, one or two lines), 📖 Why (two or three short lines), 🗣 Examples (2-3), then Uzbek (the fact in one line), 📝 Tip for learners (replaces IELTS tip), Mini task. Only facts widely documented in dictionaries or linguistics references; never popular myths.
